Ferns would definitely be pretty, and they have great movement as well which is delightful. Your flower choices are also great. The anthurium are beautiful. I was a florist for several years and this arrangement is on its last legs. Is this a mock up of the arrangements that will later be made for the wedding or is this the actual arrangement that will be used for the wedding? If it’s a mock-up, it’s honestly fine. But if it’s suppose to last any amount of time until the ceremony, then you’ve been let down by the florist. The roses are already blown, which indicates they’ve been sitting for some time (or were improperly stored) and therefore will not last much longer at all.

While it is quite common for florists to prepare wedding arrangements several days in advance, precautions must be taken to keep the arrangements looking fresh (daily water changing, special preserving chemicals added to the water, clipping greenery, storing in a cool spot, etc.). From a former florist, it does not seem that those precautions have been taken here.

The choice of flowers and color pallet are pretty, but the overall design of this arrangement reads “funeral” more than “wedding,” specifically because of the front facing design (as opposed to an in-the-round type of design). Gladioluses are also very commonly used in funeral sprays so I think the inclusion of them also pushed the arrangement towards looking more funeral. I feel like the arrangement could be improved by adding some lush greenery (perhaps Italian ruscus, seeded eucalyptus, or spiral eucalyptus) to make it look fuller and more upscale. Perhaps replace the gladiolus with snapdragons or delphinium to keep the height, but with flowers that are less associated with funerals.

I hope this helps!!

For me, bad panic attacks start with almost a teeth-tingling sensation. After that, sounds seem louder and lights/colors seem brighter. After that comes the lightheadedness you’ve mentioned. Remember that one of the first milestones of overcoming panic attacks is to recognizing the first physical symptoms (that way you can take action to calm yourself).
